* Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team and creating innovative process improvement initiatives. * The Nurse Manager is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the 24/7 operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other NMs as needed. * The NM is responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance. * They function as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team. * They enhance care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes. * The NM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth. * They adhere to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. * They equip staff with tools for lifestyle competent care and promotes a lifestyle of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes. * They cultivate alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. * The NM contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care. * Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards. * Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. * They promote an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission. * The NM maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP).

The Nurse Manager (NM) functions as a clinical expert and is responsible for all aspects of the nursing process when providing or supervising patient care. They assess, plan, implement, and evaluate care based on age-specific needs.

They coordinate care with a focus on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction across the continuum of care. By collaborating with the interdisciplinary team and developing innovative process improvement initiatives, they positively influence care outcomes.

The Nurse Manager will have oversite of ASC/ASU/Pre-anesthesia/PACU/PICC Team/Neuromodulation Clinic/Pain Management Clinic/Ketamine Clinic/and Interventional Radiology. Duties include but not limited to the following: Engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth.

Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Equips staff with tools for culturally competent care and promotes a culture of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

Cultivates alliances across the care continuum, building trust through active listening, engagement, and emotional intelligence. Contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable, and equitable patient care. Ensures compliance with accreditation and regulatory standards.

Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Promotes an inclusive workplace valuing diversity to achieve the organizations vision and mission. Preferred Experience: Knowledge of ambulatory and inpatient procedural processes. 3-5 years Peri-Operative experience required.

Knowledge of the National Patient Safety Goals as stated by Joint Commission. Superior communication skills to ignite interdisciplinary collaboration. 2-3 years of experience supervising staff. Demonstrated healthcare leadership experience in expanding scope preferred.

Experience in data analysis for evaluation and improvement of performance metrics. Demonstrated success in outcome improvement.

The function of the Registered Nurse Evidence Base Practice Coordinator (EBPC) is to serve as a leader in change process for the promotion of sustainable outcomes; demonstrates a leadership role in enhancing group dynamics, process skills, and facilitating team decision making by using decision tools related to EBP.

The EBPC fosters the integration of nursing and evidence-based best practice, which includes the translation of research finding into improving patient outcomes by the implementation and evaluation of EBP. Performs comprehensive microsystem assessment to provide the context for problem identification, and action by the utilization of EBP.

(a) Leading and organizing delivery of care to assure continuity of care and peer accountability for practice, including access to care and discharge planning; (b) Using advanced clinical knowledge/judgment to promote staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes, (c) Functioning as an expert in clinical practice and/or areas related to the assigned roles and responsibilities, (d) Systematically evaluating current practice, and formulating outcomes for groups of patients and/or organizational processes within an area of expertise, (e) Guiding, developing, and supporting staff from a leadership perspective, and (f) Using professional standards of care, scientific evidence, and practice to evaluate programs and/or service activities.

Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Provides administrative and clinical leadership for the Referral Coordination Program (RCP), ensuring effective coordination of referral management activities across the organization.

Oversees the coordination, implementation, and continuous improvement of clinical referral management processes to ensure timely, appropriate, and Veteran-centered care.

Serves as the liaison between Surgery Service, specialty providers, nursing staff, administrative personnel, and leadership to facilitate efficient referral coordination and communication.

Supervises nursing and clinical staff by planning work assignments, establishing priorities, monitoring workload distribution, and ensuring efficient daily operations.

Ensures nursing care and referral management activities comply with Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Community Care (OCC), accreditation, regulatory, and professional practice standards.

Leads quality improvement initiatives by analyzing referral management data, monitoring program performance metrics, identifying trends, and recommending operational improvements.

Develops, revises, and implements standard operating procedures, policies, and workflows in response to changes in national directives, OCC guidance, VISN requirements, and facility policies. Collaborates with physicians, specialty consultants, and interdisciplinary teams to improve clinical coordination, referral processes, and patient outcomes.

Reviews clinical documentation to ensure compliance with Referral Coordination Initiative requirements, regulatory standards, and organizational policies. Monitors program performance through data analysis, prepares reports and presentations, and provides recommendations to executive leadership for process improvement.

Recruits, interviews, selects, mentors, and develops staff while collaborating with Human Resources to support timely hiring and workforce planning. Evaluates employee performance by establishing expectations, conducting competency assessments, completing performance evaluations, and providing ongoing coaching and feedback.

Identifies staff educational needs and coordinates orientation, continuing education, competency validation, and mandatory training to support professional development and regulatory compliance.

Addresses employee relations matters by resolving workplace concerns, counseling staff, recommending disciplinary actions when appropriate, and ensuring adherence to labor relations and Equal Employment Opportunity requirements.

Ensures exceptional customer service by promoting Veteran-centered care, improving patient satisfaction, and supporting safe, respectful, and equitable healthcare delivery.

Maintains operational readiness by monitoring compliance with accreditation standards, patient safety initiatives, infection prevention practices, and organizational performance requirements.

Performs referral management and clinical review activities to maintain subject matter expertise, identify operational barriers, and support efficient patient access to specialty care.

Participates in facility, VISN, and interdisciplinary committees, task forces, and workgroups to advance nursing practice, referral coordination, and organizational initiatives. Analyzes current and future workforce requirements to determine staffing needs, competency requirements, and resource allocation to meet program objectives.

Provides leadership coverage for senior Referral Coordination Program management as assigned and performs other related duties necessary to support organizational and patient care objectives.

CTVHCS is in the process of making a cultural change, shifting from a disease-focused approach to a health and wellbeing approach, in order to implement the Whole Health System of Care. This is a VA-wide initiative to provide a comprehensive and systematic approach to improve healthcare delivery at all stages of Veteran care.

This entails moving from an episodic, "siloed" approach to an interdisciplinary, holistic approach, emphasizing self-care in the larger context of well-being.

All staff in this facility will be part of this process, shifting the focus from the question, "What's the matter with you?" to the question, "What matters to you, and how can we help you live your best life?" This strategy also involves integrating a full range of conventional approaches with Complementary and Integrative Health (CIH) approaches in order to optimize lifelong health and well-being, as defined by the Veteran, rather than narrowly focusing on disease management.

The Acute Psychiatric Nurse duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to the following: Provides and leads the provision of competent, evidence-based care, the psychiatric mental health (MH) nurse independently provides patient-centered and recovery-oriented care, milieu management, and maintains self-awareness while caring for patients living with MH conditions.

Facilitate shift reports, warm hand-offs, and nurse-led psychoeducational groups. Use therapeutic communication techniques. Practice de-escalation techniques. Utilize recovery-oriented language. Actively participates in MH interdisciplinary treatment team & MH Environment of Care rounds. Assumes team lead for psychiatric emergencies.

Reports and assists in resolving safety concerns. Documents nursing assessments, nursing plan of care, patient safety observations, and environmental safety rounds according to facility policy. Maintains professional boundaries to protect patient vulnerabilities and act in the best interest of the patient.

Has oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting. Assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization consultation. Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the MH interdisciplinary team. Supports colleagues through MH knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Shares MH educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based MH practice culture.

### Der Beruf im Detail: Was macht eine diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH?
Als diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH tragen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung über den ganzen Pflegeprozess. Sie erheben den Pflegebedarf, danach planen Sie die Massnahmen und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Zudem steuern Sie die Abgabe der Medikamente, überwachen Vitalzeichen und erkennen Veränderungen früh. Damit sichern Sie Tag für Tag die Qualität der Pflege.
Der Weg in diesen Beruf führt über die höhere Fachschule (HF) oder das Bachelorstudium Pflege (FH). Ausländische Diplome brauchen dafür eine [Anerkennung durch das Schweizerische Rote Kreuz (SRK)](https://www.redcross.ch/de/srk-anerkennung). Ausserdem stehen erfahrenen Fachpersonen viele Wege offen: ein Nachdiplomstudium (NDS), die Rolle als Berufsbildnerin oder die Teamleitung.
Der Arbeitsmarkt in der Region Niederglatt zeigt eine hohe Nachfrage nach diplomierten Pflegefachfrauen und -männern HF/FH, insbesondere für Bezugspflegeaufträge im 80-100%-Pensum.

Major components of this function include surveillance, prevention and control activities; reporting communicable illnesses; infection control policy development; administrative functions; infection control education and training; consultative services, and analysis of infection control data.

The Infection Preventionist (IP) has the authority to function in all services of the organization to coordinate, establish and monitor acceptable infection control practices and standards.

S/he serves as a principal member of the Infection Control Committee and recommends new or revised practices, based on currently accepted evidence-based infection prevention and control strategies.

The IP evaluates clinical parameters to determine the presence of infection, assess the severity of disease, identify specific risk factors, and determine source(s) for infection that can be improved.

The IP analyzes surveillance data monthly, quarterly, and annually to identify unusual occurrences, clusters of infection, infection due to unusual pathogens, and occurrence of healthcare-acquired infections that exceed the targets established for the organization, determining the need for intervention.

The IP uses standard definitions for the identification and classification of events, indicators, or outcomes and appropriate statistical techniques to describe the data, calculate rates and critically evaluate the significance of findings.

The IP analyzes data using comparative data when available and reports epidemiologically significant findings appropriately. The IP evaluates infectiousness of patients and employees with communicable diseases, makes recommendations for isolation or work restrictions, and investigates exposures to these diseases.

The IP recognizes deviations from infection control standards and makes recommendations as necessary to maintain the same level of infection control prevention and control standards throughout all areas of the organization.

The IP evaluates the effectiveness of infection prevention and control measures in assigned areas of responsibility and identifies potential infection hazards and deviations from expected hospital target for infection and/or colonization of patients.

The IP facilitates implementation of infection control policies and procedures and makes recommendations for integration of infection control principles throughout the medical center. The IP monitors implementation of infection control policies and procedures.

The IP identifies opportunities to integrate surveillance findings into the organization's plan for improvement and initiates and facilitates procedural changes to improve infection control practices through active participation and/or collaboration with appropriate committees or workgroups.

The IP takes remedial action and implements immediate infection control measures when a known breach is identified or there is reason to believe that there is danger of exposure to or spread of infection in patients or personnel. The IP communicates and follows up with all services involved to ensure corrective action is implemented.

The IP formulates individual goals for specific areas of individual responsibility to accomplish the broader goals of the Infection Control Program. The IP participates in Quality Improvement activities and contributes epidemiological skills and expert knowledge of infection prevention and control methods.

The IP uses knowledge of current scientific literature and existing regulations and guidelines to incorporate appropriate recommendations into written infection control policies and procedures and to ensure consistency with current standards of care.

The IP establishes and maintains effective oral and written communications with all services and community agencies as needed concerning prevention and control of infections in patients. The IP ensures that findings, recommendations, and policies of the infection control program are disseminated to appropriate individuals.
